title: Cohorted Burst Oracle & Staged Handoff — PRD (draft)
content:
Overview:

This PRD describes the Cohorted Burst Oracle (CBO) and Staged Handoff pattern for Dedicated pools. The goal is to provide a predictable, low-latency burst experience while reducing noisy-neighbor risk by treating groups of tenants (cohorts) as first-class scheduling units. We combine short-horizon demand signals, tenant-declared intents, and conservative ML smoothing to seed warm resources and execute staged handoffs that maintain isolation guarantees.

Why this is different / problem statement:
- Current per-tenant burst models either (a) over-provision broadly (costly) or (b) rely on opportunistic borrowing which can expose high-priority tenants to latency tail events.
- We need a mechanism that "looks sideways" across similar tenants to amortize warm costs, while retaining the ability to quarantine or throttle cohorts when isolation risk rises.
- Existing designs in the repo focus heavily on credit pools or one-off warm-pools; CBO brings cohort-aware prediction + staged, observable handoff that is easier for SRE and support to reason about.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce 95th percentile tail latency impact from burst events for high-SLO tenants by >= 30% in 6 months (relative to baseline).
- Reduce incremental burst warm GPU-hours per peak-day by >= 20% via cohort sharing vs naive per-tenant warm allocation.
- Provide deterministic isolation controls: ability to fully quarantine a cohort within 60s of detection and to roll back staged handoff within 10s.
- Operational clarity: provide a single dashboard surface showing cohort health, warm budget, and active handoffs.

Non-goals:
- Replace per-tenant reservation system — tenants can still purchase Dedicated reservations. CBO augments burst economics.
- Full ML-driven autoscaling replacement — CBO is a short-horizon demand predictor (minutes scale) combined with policy rules.

User scenarios / user stories:
- As an SRE, I want to see which cohorts are being warmed and why, and immediately stop a handoff if a noisy tenant appears.
- As a platform engineer, I want the system to pre-warm GPU slots for an upcoming campaign announced by a tenant (tenant-declared intent) and to amortize warm time across a cohort of similar tenants.
- As a product owner, I want burst costs to be predictable and capped per cohort so we can bill and report cleanly.

Solution sketch:
1) Cohort definition: a lightweight label set assigned at account-level (e.g., app-type:web-search, model:embedding-v2, tier:enterprise). Cohorts are dynamic (auto-join on similarity signals) but can be pinned by customer opt-in.

2) Short-horizon Demand Oracle: ensemble predictor combining:
   - recent request-rate/time-series (per-tenant and cohort-aggregated)
   - queued rate growth (from API gateway metrics)
   - tenant-declared intents (scheduled jobs, webhooks)
   - calendar/context signals (timezone, campaign tags)
   Output: a per-cohort demand curve for the next 0-30 minutes with confidence bands.

3) Warm budget & staged handoff:
   - Each cohort has a warm budget (GPU-minutes) that can be pre-funded or consumed on demand.
   - Staged handoff phases: pre-warm -> partial-supply -> full-supply. Each phase emits telemetry and a reversible state change.
   - Partial-supply routes a percentage of cohort traffic to warmed nodes while still serving a fraction on cold paths (controls latency risk).

4) Isolation & honor system:
   - Quarantine mode: when a tenant exhibits noisy behavior (burst beyond cohort thresholds, bad tail latency), CBO can immediately throttle that tenant and shift cohort warm to other members.
   - Honor system: tenants may opt-in to a cooperative pool with contractual caps; those who opt-out get explicit isolation and cannot borrow cohort warm. Honor system state affects prediction priors and cost allocation.

5) Policy layer & fallback:
   - Policies live in the console: priority weighting, max-borrow %, quarantine thresholds, billing caps.
   - Fallback: if cohort warm is exhausted, system falls back to pre-configured compatible model variants (lower-cost quantized variants) or regional fallback lanes.

API / Console changes (brief):
- New API endpoints: POST /cohorts (create/pin), GET /cohorts/{id}/forecast, POST /cohorts/{id}/manual-handoff
- Console: Cohort dashboard card with forecast sparkline, warm budget, active handoffs table, and manual revoke button.
- Alerts: cohort-warm-depleted, cohort-noisy-tenant-detected, staged-handoff-failed.

Telemetry & SLOs to track:
- Latency p50/p90/p95 for tenants before/during/after handoff
- Cohort warm utilization (GPU-minutes used vs forecasted)
- Handoff reversal time (target <= 10s)
- Quarantine action frequency and false-positive rate (ops override ratio)
- Cost delta (cohort vs per-tenant warm baseline)

Operational playbook (high-level):
- Normal flow: Oracle forecasts > threshold -> system pre-warms -> staged handoff auto-executes -> cohort observes lower tail latency.
- Noisy tenant flows: detection -> auto-quarantine tenant -> adjust cohort allocation -> notify tenant & CSE.
- Emergency rollback: manual revoke in console or POST /cohorts/{id}/revoke -> system migrates served traffic back to cold lane with rate-limited draining.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiments): 2 months. Run from a canary cluster with 5 internal tenants; no billing or public cohorts. Telemetry validation.
- Phase 1 (opt-in beta): 8 weeks. Invite 10 external customers across tiers to opt-in to cohort sharing. Offer credits to offset risk.
- Phase 2 (guarded launch): 12 weeks. Wider availability; default cohort suggestions in console; strict quotas on warm budgets.
- Phase 3 (GA): after metrics targets met and SRE runbook hardened.

Risks & mitigation:
- Over-sharing warm capacity can amplify noisy neighbors: mitigation = honor system opt-out + fast quarantine + per-tenant throttles.
- Forecasting false positives waste warm hours: mitigation = conservative priors + cost-aware threshold and decay windows.
- Billing disputes from shared cost: mitigation = detailed per-tenant chargeback logs and a cohort ledger view.

Open questions / research items:
- Best similarity features for cohorting (model family vs traffic pattern vs account tags) — needs A/B experiments.
- How large should cohorts be before diminishing returns? (cost/benefit curve).
- SLA semantics for opt-in cohorts (what do we guarantee?).

Next steps & owners:
- Prototype Oracle + UI mockups (owner: Liam O'Neill) — 3 weeks to first prototype.
- Smallscale canary run with 3 internal tenants (owner: Sofia Martinez) — 6 weeks.
- Design billing ledger schema and hooks (owner: Noah Patel) — 4 weeks.

Notes to self (working items / TODOs):
- Add sequence diagrams for staged handoff and rollback.
- Draft SRE runbook with concrete escalation steps and telemetry thresholds.
- Prepare partner-facing FAQ explaining honor system and opt-in implications.

References and context:
- Related: predictive-warm-pool-orchestrator-and-borrowing-prd-draft.json (see concept overlap but cohort-first approach differs)
- See JIRA-DCAP-482 for initial demand signals backlog and gh://redwood-inference/infra/pull/2214 for the warm-pool task queue change.
